citations.quote: This was a randomized, controlled, multicenter, double-masked, parallel group, Phase 2b/3 study designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of lotilaner ophthalmic solution in the treatment of *Demodex* blepharitis.

Subjects were randomized (1:1) to receive either lotilaner ophthalmic solution or vehicle. The study drugs were masked with subjects instructed to instill a single drop of the assigned study drug twice daily (morning and evening) in each eye. The study drug administration period was 43 days (approximately 6 weeks).

citations.quote: XDEMVY is indicated for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis.

target_moa.text: Lotilaner is an isoxazoline ectoparasiticide that inhibits mite GABA-gated chloride channels, blocking chloride ion transfer across cell membranes and causing uncontrolled neuromuscular activity and spastic paralysis of Demodex mites.

citations.quote: Lotilaner is a member of the isoxazoline family of compounds. Isoxazolines are inhibitors of mite \gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-gated chloride channels. This inhibition blocks the transfer of chloride ions across cell membranes, which results in uncontrolled neuromuscular activity. Ectoparasites exposed to isoxazolines will exhibit a spastic paralysis.
Lotilaner is an ectoparasiticide and insecticide initially developed as a veterinary product for control of flea and tick infestations and has also been found effective against Demodex mites.

Tarsus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Tarsus) submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) for XDEMVY™ (Lotilaner Ophthalmic Solution, 0.25%) through the 505(b)(1) pathway for approval. XDEMVY is indicated for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis.

key_safety.text: Most common ocular adverse reaction was instillation site stinging and burning (10%); other ocular reactions reported in <2% of patients were chalazion/hordeolum and punctate keratitis. Evaluated in 833 patients across Saturn-1 and Saturn-2; no deaths occurred.

citations.quote: XDEMVY was evaluated in 833 patients with Demodex blepharitis in two randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled studies (Saturn-1 and Saturn-2) with 42 days of treatment. The most common ocular adverse reaction observed in controlled clinical studies with XDEMVY was instillation site stinging and burning which was reported in 10% of patients. Other ocular adverse reactions reported in less than 2% of patients were chalazion/hordeolum and punctate keratitis.
No deaths occurred in the two pivotal studies included in the clinical development program for lotilaner ophthalmic solution in the treatment of Demodex blepharitis.
